subject: [PATCH 3/9] mm/gup: convert follow_page_mask() to return a long

2026-11-23.patch_summary: This patch changes the return type of follow_page_mask() and its helpers from a struct page pointer to a long integer. The new return value can be an error code, 0 indicating no page found, or 1 with the page stored in a pages[0] slot. This allows the function to carry a page count rather than a single page pointer.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David suggested reworking the patch to collect all folio pages directly within the follow_page_mask() and its helpers, rather than returning a long value.

Reviewer David pointed out that the term 'subpages' should be avoided in favor of 'remaining pages', citing Willy's repeated statement on this matter.

Reviewer David suggested using gup_fill_pages() in the no_page_table function, and questioned the necessity of calling it again in the fill_flush path.

Reviewer David suggested rebasing the patch on top of mm-core/for-next, as it recently changed slightly and will introduce some smaller conflicts, but nothing earth-shattering. He also wondered if converting some functions before follow_page_mask() would be feasible.
reviews.raw_body:
You can say here that we will rework that next, to collect all folio pages from
inside these functions directly.

---

As willy keeps saying, there is no such thing as subpages.

"a large folio's remainin pages"

---

Why not use gup_fill_pages() here?

But why do we goto fill_flush where we do another gup_fill_pages?

---

This code recently changed slightly:

commit 2d9bcd380585abc436f055fbb618b34f98882004
Author: David Hildenbrand (Arm) <david@kernel.org>
Date:   Thu Nov 12 23:53:24 2026 +0100

    mm/gup: limit pagecache folio refcount when grabbing references

So once you rebase on top of mm-core/for-next, there will be some smaller
conflcits but nothign earth shattering.


There is a lot happening in this patch. I wonder if there would be some way to
convert some of the functions before converting follow_page_mask().

-- 
Cheers,

David

2026-11-26.patch_summary: This patch changes the return type of follow_page_mask() and its helper functions from a struct page pointer to a long integer. The long integer can hold either an error code, a count of pages found, or a special value indicating that a single page was stored in a new pages[0] slot. This change allows for more efficient handling of large folios and their subpages. No functional changes are intended by this patch.
